summary: Bootmod3 maps, exhaust flap, Active Sound and burbles in iDrive 6
author: inotbarnacle (packaged by NBTApps)
description:
A menu under My Vehicle for a car with a bootmod3 CustomROM tune: it asks the engine control unit (DME) to switch maps and to change the exhaust flap, Active Sound and burbles.

What it does
- Maps 1 to 4 on the main page, which reads the active map when it opens and after each selection
- OPTIONS opens Exhaust flap, Active Sound and Burbles, with three burble presets
- For maps and burbles it finds out which CustomROM the DME has, and where that ROM keeps them. With a ROM it does not know, those are switched off
- Maps and burble presets are written to the DME's memory and read back. Exhaust flap and Active Sound are fixed commands that work without that lookup, and show whether the DME acknowledged the request

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6), on a software version the app was built for (see Good to know)
- NBTApps agent 1.6.0 or later
- The car's diagnostic gateway. The app tries 169.254.21.3, and if nothing answers there, looks for the gateway on the car's wired network
- A bootmod3 CustomROM tune that the app knows. The tune and the car's hardware decide which requests work

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open My Vehicle and choose Bootmod3 Suite.

Good to know
- It cannot be installed together with MHD+ Suite: a car has one or the other
- The menu writes to the engine control unit. Try each command first with the car parked
- The burble presets need the diagnostic gateway. The rest can fall back to the car's MOST bus
- The page is laid out for the screen when the package is installed: 800×480, 960×480, 1280×480, 1440×540 or 1920×720. If the screen's size cannot be read, the 1280×480 layout is used
- Owners report that on some cars the app only gets data while a device is plugged into the OBD port
- This package does not check the head unit's software version. The author's own installer checks the head unit's iDrive framework files, and accepts those of these NBTevo versions only: K17052I, L17252I, M17345I, M17365I, N18032I, N18092I, O18184I, P18362I, Q18491I, R19101I, R19144I, S19221I, S19322I, T18501I, T21424I, T23235J, T24081I, U19384I, V20153I, W20204I, X20511I, Y21432J, Y22292I, Y23236I and Y24073J. On another version the menu may not load
- If the app was put on this car before, with the author's desktop installer or by hand, uninstall it the same way first. NBTApps refuses to install over it
- If the app does not find the car's diagnostic gateway, put its address in a gateway-ip.txt file on the head unit: /var/opt/hmi/data/ID5/gateway-ip.txt for all of the author's apps at once, or one in the app's own folder. The shared file comes first. This package writes neither
- This is a pre-release: the package has not yet been installed on a car through NBTApps

Bootmod3 Suite is by inotbarnacle, free of charge under the MIT License. Its bootmod3 commands come from the idrive7-apps project, whose licence is in the package. NBTApps packages the author's own builds, unchanged, with the author's agreement. It comes as it is: you install it at your own risk.
